note: Independent whole-clause rejudgment against RFC 9830 §2.3: "The Tunnel Egress Endpoint and Color sub-TLVs of the Tunnel Encapsulation Attribute, as defined in [RFC9012], are not utilized for SR Policy encodings. Consequently, their values are not relevant within the context of the SR Policy SAFI NLRI. If these sub-TLVs are present, a BGP speaker MUST ignore them and MAY remove them from the Tunnel Encapsulation Attribute during propagation." The current summary has no partial/gap annotation for this requirement. All four current tags were read: both polarities in reactor TestRFC9830InapplicableSubTLVsIgnoredOnReceipt and attribute TestRFC9830EgressEndpointAndColorSubTLVsIgnored. The reactor's positive cases compare a clean policy with individually added endpoint and Color sub-TLVs on actual AFI 1/73 and 2/73 carriers, requiring no error, exactly RFC7606ActionNone, unchanged MP_REACH including its NLRI and next hop, one retained type-15 tunnel, and readable Preference 100. Its negative controls add duplicate endpoints or an endpoint with a one-octet value and require the same outcomes, catching erroneous application of unicast endpoint-count/value validation to an SR Policy. These inputs isolate applicability: teSub/teTLV encode their actual lengths, so the short endpoint has invalid endpoint content but intact sub-TLV and outer framing; teSRPolicyBody supplies a single type-15 TLV, correctly sized policy NLRI, ORIGIN, four-octet AS_SEQUENCE 65002 and an IPv4-format Route Target, with no legacy announcement. The attribute positive control reads equal Preference values with and without endpoint/Color; its separate negative control changes the applicable Preference from 4242 to 9999 and requires a changed result, excluding blanket disregard of all sub-TLVs. Round-trip equality additionally pins Ze's permitted retention choice. Source inspection confirms applyRFC7606 calls applyTunnelEncap and consumes both returned values; applyTunnelEncap identifies the policy from MP_REACH AFI/SAFI, and tunnelTLVLayout still validates framing but skips endpoint semantic/count checks when policy is true and assigns no meaning to Color. TunnelTLV.Preference consumes only type 12 with the required six-octet value; its readback is a codec assertion, not evidence of SRPM selection. processValidatedMessage forwards accepted announcements through onMessageReceived; notifyMessageReceiver caches the accepted WireUpdate before dispatch. teForwardedAttrs exercises that real receive/cache/ForwardUpdate path to an iBGP socket and a downstream processMessage consumer, both without the MED policy and with an actual MED=50 rebuild, asserting preserved attributes/MP_REACH, one announcement and no synthesized withdrawal. Ignoring these contents does not require erasing their wire bytes: byte retention is a conforming implementation choice under MAY, not an additional RFC MUST. Stored native records for this reactor cover name replacement of applyTunnelEncap by panic; those establish sensitivity to that producer halt only, not selective endpoint/Color discrimination. Historical records naming the former carry-test cover likewise do not extend current semantic proof. No checks, mutations, hashes or canonical edits were performed for this rejudgment. Credit is limited to the implemented receive, codec and cached propagation behavior demonstrated by these assertions; no separate route-server rail, SR Policy Manager, attribute-driven steering or dataplane proof is claimed, and absent consumers remain separately unimplemented scope. RFC9830-2.3-3 is not rejudged. No code map is needed for this enforced pending entry.
